To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have investigated the electronic structure of cerium-based heavy-fermium systems, established a correlation between the parameters in x-ray photoelectron spectra, and the size of the heavy-mercury state, calculated the total and partial densities for atoms, and studied the influence of an x-ray-induced inner level vacancy on the shape of x-ray photoelectron Ce3d spectra.

the heavy-fermmion state in cerium-based systems is related to the degree of hybridization of the f electrons with the outer shell electrons, and the magnitude of this state is proportional to the intensity of the satellite in the Ce 3d spectra.
the electronic structure of the cerium-based heavy fermions is sensitive to the degree of f-electron hybridization and to pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the external effects on the properties of Ce-based heavy fermions.
a theoretical and experimental investigation of electronic properties of Ce compounds and the effect of an inner-level vacancy on XPS spectra.
theoretical and experimental investigation of heavy-fermions and the effect of external effects on their electronic structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shakedown satellites are the most reliable indicators of the heavy- fermion state.
the magnitude of hybridization and the magnitude of heavy-fermions state are not directly proportional to each other.

Ce3d spectra can be used to investigate the degree of covalence and the magnitude of hybridization of 4f electrons with outer-shell states, the magnitude of the Kondo effect and the degree of localization of 4f states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a correlation between the parameters in the X-ray photoelectron spectrum and the magnitude of a heavy-fermionic state is established and that the heavy-fermic state decreases with pressure.

the magnitude of hybridization of the f electrons with outer electrons is the main factor that determines the magnitude of the hybridization gap, the degree of localization of the 4f electrons, and the magnitude of heavy-fermions.
the heavy-ferminon state of Ce systems is determined by the degree of covalence of the f-electrons with the outer electrons and the magnitude of this state decreases under pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray photoelectron spectrum of a heavy-fermionic system can be a sensitive indicator of its electronic properties.
X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy can be used to study the electronic structure of heavy-fermionic systems.

we have shown the relationship between the magnitude and the nature of the Ce3+ state and the magnitude of hybridization of the f electrons with outer shell electrons, and the possibility of using the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy method to study the effect of an induced vacancy in the Ce4f shell.
